description:
Implement two features in the Zonoid orchestrator at /Users/imyu/Desktop/zonoid: ## Feature 1: Progress heartbeat via classify.sh The classifier (hooks/classify.sh) already injects instructions into the main agent on every UserPromptSubmit. Add a heartbeat instruction: 1. In daemon.js: add `report_interval_seconds` to the overlay config defaults (default: 300). The existing `POST /config` endpoint already merges arbitrary fields — no new route needed. Add a `GET /config` route (or expose the existing config via the dashboard's data endpoint) so hooks can read it. 2. In classify.sh: after building the existing context output, read `report_interval_seconds` from `GET localhost:$PORT/config`. Adjust it based on the routing decision already computed: - decision=workflow or many in-flight tasks → multiply by 0.67 (tighten), floor at 60s - decision=solo/simple → multiply by 1.33 (relax) - Clamp to [60, 3600] Add this line to the additionalContext output: `"If tasks are in flight, use ScheduleWakeup({delaySeconds: X, reason: 'progress heartbeat', prompt: 'Report progress on in-flight orchestrator tasks: call show_dashboard, summarize what completed and what is still running, then reschedule the next heartbeat.'}) after responding."` 3. In public/graph.html settings popup (around line 260-272): add a dropdown for the heartbeat interval before the Save button: ```html
Progress heartbeat
How often the main agent auto-reports in-flight task progress
``` Wire it into toggleSettingsPopup (load saved value into dropdown) and saveSettings (save to localStorage + POST /config {report_interval_seconds: value}). ## Feature 2: Completion notice via Stop hook When a subagent finishes and the main agent responds, the Stop hook should surface what just completed. 1. In daemon.js: add a `/completed-since` endpoint. It accepts `?session=SID&since=TIMESTAMP` and returns tasks that moved to done/failed since that timestamp, with their labels and brief summaries. Also add `/completed-since/ack` (POST) that records the last-acked timestamp per session. 2. Create hooks/stop-report.sh: fires on the Stop hook event. Reads last-ack timestamp for this session from daemon, calls `/completed-since`, if any tasks completed emits additionalContext: `"[Orchestrator] Tasks completed since your last response: "`. 3. Wire stop-report.sh into .claude/settings.json Stop hook. ## Constraints - Call start_task on the task assigned to you BEFORE editing any files (gate requirement) - The daemon source is at /Users/imyu/Desktop/zonoid/daemon.js - Hooks live at /Users/imyu/Desktop/zonoid/hooks/ but are symlinked from /Users/imyu/.claude/orchestrator/hooks/ — edit the zonoid/hooks/ originals - settings.json is at /Users/imyu/Desktop/zonoid/.claude/settings.json - Match existing code style exactly - Do not restart the daemon (disruptive — user will do it) --- From Learner queue: batch-process all candidates with cursor, no upfront cap: Build a queue-based multi-step processing mode for /Users/imyu/.claude/orchestrator/scripts/onboard-learn.js, modeled on the judge cursor pattern. Problem: the current --max-candidates cap is architecturally wrong — on large repos (cosma-ai-studio: 2457 candidates), the cap destroys coverage (150 kept only 20 notes, kb_earned 13%). Fix: (1) New subcommand/flag: onboard-learn.js --enqueue --out reads all mined notes from --in and writes a queue file (/onboard-queue.json: {pending:[...all candidates...], kept:[], rejected:[], cursor:0, total:N}). (2) onboard-learn.js --drain --batch 50 --out : reads queue, processes the next --batch candidates through the existing LLM keep/reject logic, updates kept/rejected/cursor in place, exits. Re-runnable: safe to call repeatedly until cursor==total. (3) onboard-learn.js --inject --confirm can already work from onboard-notes.json; after drain completes write final onboard-notes.json from queue.kept as before. (4) Add --queue-status flag: prints {total, processed:cursor, kept:len(kept), remaining:total-cursor, done:cursor==total}. (5) Remove --max-candidates or keep it as a hard emergency cap only (default: none). Follow orch-gate: write to /tmp, cp into place. Branch orch/attempt/learner-queue off main in /Users/imyu/.claude/orchestrator, add tests (test/learner-queue.test.js style), run full suite + smoke.sh green, then merge to main. Do NOT restart the daemon. Summary of what you built goes to complete_task on the graph task key provided in your context — use the HTTP API (POST http://localhost:8787/overlay/status with workspace=/Users/imyu/Desktop/cloude) since MCP workspace resolution may be stale until daemon restart. --- From Manually apply gated-DAG patch to daemon.js: Apply the gated-DAG patch to /Users/imyu/Desktop/zonoid/daemon.js. Implement two features in the Zonoid orchestrator at /Users/imyu/Desktop/zonoid: ## Feature 1: Progress heartbeat via classify.sh The classifier (hooks/classify.sh) already injects instructions into the main agent on every UserPromptSubmit. Add a heartbeat instruction: 1. In daemon.js: add `report_interval_seconds` to the overlay config defaults (default: 300). The existing `POST /config` endpoint already merges arbitrary fields — no new route needed. Add a `GET /config` route (or expose the existing config via the dashboard's data endpoint) so hooks can read it. 2. In classify.sh: after building the existing context output, read `report_interval_seconds` from `GET localhost:$PORT/config`. Adjust it based on the routing decision already computed: - decision=workflow or many in-flight tasks → multiply by 0.67 (tighten), floor at 60s - decision=solo/simple → multiply by 1.33 (relax) - Clamp to [60, 3600] Add this line to the additionalContext output: `"If tasks are in flight, use ScheduleWakeup({delaySeconds: X, reason: 'progress heartbeat', prompt: 'Report progress on in-flight orchestrator tasks: call show_dashboard, summarize what completed and what is still running, then reschedule the next heartbeat.'}) after responding."` 3. In public/graph.html settings popup (around line 260-272): add a dropdown for the heartbeat interval before the Save button: ```html
Progress heartbeat
How often the main agent auto-reports in-flight task progress
``` Wire it into toggleSettingsPopup (load saved value into dropdown) and saveSettings (save to localStorage + POST /config {report_interval_seconds: value}). ## Feature 2: Completion notice via Stop hook When a subagent finishes and the main agent responds, the Stop hook should surface what just completed. 1. In daemon.js: add a `/completed-since` endpoint. It accepts `?session=SID&since=TIMESTAMP` and returns tasks that moved to done/failed since that timestamp, with their labels and brief summaries.
